title: Compatible finite-presentation stalk models and induced fibre stalk maps
statement:
Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$ and $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$, assume $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and fix $x\in X$, $y=f(x)$, $s=p(x)$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\alpha=q_y^\sharp:R\to B$, $\beta=f_x^\sharp:B\to C$ for their stalk maps [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and $\mathfrak m_R$ for the maximal ideal of $R$. Then these are nonzero local rings, the two maps are local, meaning that they send maximal ideals into maximal ideals, and $\beta\alpha=p_x^\sharp$.

There exist an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ containing $s$, affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset X$ containing $x$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}E\subset Y$ containing $y$, with $p(U),q(W)\subset V$, and primes $\mathfrak a\subset A$, $\mathfrak c\subset D$, $\mathfrak b\subset E$ representing $s,x,y$, such that $D$ is finitely presented over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $E$ is of finite type over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and the germ identifications $R\cong A_{\mathfrak a}$, $C\cong D_{\mathfrak c}$, $B\cong E_{\mathfrak b}$ identify $p_x^\sharp,q_y^\sharp$ with the corresponding localized ring maps [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $P=R\otimes_A D$ and $Q=R\otimes_A E$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The algebras $P,Q$ are respectively finitely presented and of finite type over $R$; the maps from $D,E$ to them exhibit localization at the respective images of $A\setminus\mathfrak a$. The induced maps $P\to C$, $r\otimes d\mapsto p_x^\sharp(r)d_x$, and $Q\to B$, $r\otimes e\mapsto\alpha(r)e_y$, exhibit further localizations. In particular $C$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$, meaning a localization of a finitely presented $R$-algebra, and $B$ is essentially of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

Let $X_s,Y_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre], with projections $i_X,i_Y$, points $x_s,y_s$ over $x,y$, and induced map $f_s=f\times_S\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $f_s(x_s)=y_s$, the maps $[c]\mapsto i_{X,x_s}^\sharp(c)$ and $[b]\mapsto i_{Y,y_s}^\sharp(b)$ are isomorphisms $C/\mathfrak m_RC\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,x_s}$ and $B/\mathfrak m_RB\cong\mathcal O_{Y_s,y_s}$, and under them $(f_s)_{x_s}^\sharp$ is $[b]\mapsto[\beta(b)]$. Here extended ideals are generated by the images of $\mathfrak m_R$, and $\kappa(s)=R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Choose $x\in U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $s\in V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $p(U)\subset V$ and $D$ finitely presented over $A$, directly from [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For this same affine $V$, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives an affine cover of $q^{-1}(V)$ by spectra of finite type $A$-algebras; choose a member $W=\operatorname{Spec}E$ containing $y$. Write $\varphi:A\to D$ and $\psi:A\to E$ for the restricted section maps, and $\mathfrak a,\mathfrak c,\mathfrak b$ for the primes of $s,x,y$. These choices require neither $f(U)\subset W$ nor affineness of a whole inverse image.

source.place: Tag 039C (theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre), affine stalk setup; Morphisms Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation) and Tag 01T0 (definition-finite-type)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ maps identify $R=A_{\mathfrak a}$, $C=D_{\mathfrak c}$ and $B=E_{\mathfrak b}$. They are local rings; they are nonzero because $1=0$ in a prime localization would imply $t=0$ for some $t$ outside the prime, impossible by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The scheme stalk maps are local by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition](b) applied to $q\circ f=p$ gives $\beta\alpha=p_x^\sharp$. Its germ formula (a) gives $p_x^\sharp(a_s)=\varphi(a)_x$ and $\alpha(a_s)=\psi(a)_y$. Ring maps preserve inverses, so on any fraction $a/t\in A_{\mathfrak a}$ these maps are $\varphi(a)/\varphi(t)$ and $\psi(a)/\psi(t)$. Thus these are the localized ring maps in the asserted germ identifications. In particular $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak c)=\mathfrak a=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak b)$: a numerator belongs to the point's prime exactly when its germ lies in the maximal ideal, and a local homomorphism has that same inverse image (units map to units).

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), affine stalks; Sheaves Tag 008M (lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks); Schemes Tag 01HB (definition-locally-ringed-space)

proof.text: Put $P=R\otimes_A D$ and $Q=R\otimes_A E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) to $A\to D$ and $A\to R$; it says exactly that $P$ is finitely presented over $R$. For $Q$, take finite algebra generators $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $E/A$ as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Every tensor is a finite sum of $r\otimes e$, and substituting each polynomial expression $e=F(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ expresses it as an $R$-polynomial in $1\otimes e_i$. Hence those finitely many elements generate $Q/R$. This uses only the generating and balancing relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

Let $T=A\setminus\mathfrak a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its base ring and algebra both $A$, its module $M=A$, its localization $T^{-1}A=R$, and $N=D$, then $N=E$. Identify $A\otimes_A D$ with $D$ by $a\otimes d\mapsto\varphi(a)d$, inverse $d\mapsto1\otimes d$, and likewise for $E$. The lemma therefore says that $D\to P$, $d\mapsto1\otimes d$, and $E\to Q$ are localizations at the images of $T$. These are ring localizations: the module fraction formula is $d/\varphi(t)\mapsto(1/t)\otimes d$, and multiplication of these representatives is $((1/t)\otimes d)((1/u)\otimes d')=(1/(tu))\otimes dd'$. Thus it preserves $1$ and multiplication as well as addition. In particular every element of $P$ is $(1/t)\otimes d$ and every element of $Q$ is $(1/t)\otimes e$, for some $t\in T$.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), combined with Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule), as in the cited localization-over-base node

proof.text: The balancing relation defines ring maps $j:P\to C$, $r\otimes d\mapsto p_x^\sharp(r)d_x$, and $k:Q\to B$, $r\otimes e\mapsto\alpha(r)e_y$, since the two maps from $A$ agree by step 2. To check that $j$ is a further localization, let $T_D$ be the image of $D\setminus\mathfrak c$ in $P$. Its elements map to units of $C$. Every $c\in C$ is $d_x/v_x=j(1\otimes d)/j(1\otimes v)$ with $v\notin\mathfrak c$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Finally write $z\in P$ as $(1/t)\otimes d$ by step 4. If $j(z)=0$, then $d_x=0$, since $p_x^\sharp(t_s)$ is invertible. The same affine-stalk node supplies $v\notin\mathfrak c$ with $vd=0$, whence $(1\otimes v)z=0$. These are exactly the unit, fraction, and zero-kernel conditions for localization stated in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] (apply the zero case to differences for its equality condition). They prove $C=(T_D)^{-1}P$. For $k$, replace $(D,\mathfrak c,C,p_x^\sharp,d,v)$ throughout these three checks by $(E,\mathfrak b,B,\alpha,e,w)$; the identical formulas give $B=(T_E)^{-1}Q$, $T_E$ the image of $E\setminus\mathfrak b$. The displayed pure-tensor formulas ensure compatibility with the original $R$-algebra structures. By step 3 this proves the asserted essential finite presentation and, using [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], essential finite type.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction relation and successive localization checked directly; Tag 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] first to $p:X\to S$ at $x$ and then to $q:Y\to S$ at $y$. Both are scheme morphisms with the same image point $s$. The lemma gives exactly the two isomorphisms $\theta_X:C/\mathfrak m_RC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{X_s,x_s}$ and $\theta_Y:B/\mathfrak m_RB\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{Y_s,y_s}$, with $\theta_X([c])=i_{X,x_s}^\sharp(c)$ and $\theta_Y([b])=i_{Y,y_s}^\sharp(b)$. Its ideals are generated by the images of the base maximal ideal under $p_x^\sharp$ and $\alpha$, precisely the ideals here. The lemma requires no flatness, Noetherianity, finiteness, or closed-point assumption.

source.place: Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), first isomorphism, with its canonical projection map

proof.text: The defining projection identity for $f_s$ from [def-pc-fibre-product] is $i_Y\circ f_s=f\circ i_X$. Consequently $i_Y(f_s(x_s))=y$, so $f_s(x_s)=y_s$ by uniqueness of a point over $y$ in the fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition], this same identity on stalks is $(f_s)_{x_s}^\sharp\circ i_{Y,y_s}^\sharp=i_{X,x_s}^\sharp\circ\beta$. Also $\beta\alpha=p_x^\sharp$ implies $\beta(\mathfrak m_RB)\subseteq\mathfrak m_RC$: a generator $\alpha(r)b$ maps to $p_x^\sharp(r)\beta(b)$ for $r\in\mathfrak m_R$. Hence $[b]\mapsto[\beta(b)]$ is well defined. For every $b\in B$ the stalk identity gives $(f_s)_{x_s}^\sharp\theta_Y([b])=i_{X,x_s}^\sharp\beta(b)=\theta_X([\beta(b)])$. Since every quotient class has a representative, this proves the claimed identification of maps, not merely an abstract isomorphism of the fibre rings.
